revision_summary: No critical fabricated quotes were found (the two flagged items are minor ambiguity/attribution issues, not fabrications), but several issues warrant a targeted revision: (1) The 'I have a Tesla' enthusiasm_signal at ~03:18 sits right after an apparent transcription artifact ('I have a Tesla phone') — Stage 3 should either soften this to acknowledge the ambiguity or drop the upsell-sizing coaching point built on it, since it's unclear whether the customer is referencing an EV, a phone, or a garbled utterance. (2) Schema misuse: protocols.adult_child_decision_maker is cited twice (cherry_pick_moments at 02:03 and 05:33) for a scenario that is actually inverted from that protocol's definition (customer is the adult child, not the parent; parents are the potential homeowners, not co-decision-making children) — revise to either cite protocols.spouse_decision at the principle level, or better, flag this as an explicit schema gap requiring Kenny's input, and cross-reference dq_rules.not_homeowner since the customer himself may not qualify as the homeowner. (3) Add the missed moment at 01:56 where the rep's own system data ('which I have you here as [homeowner]') conflicts with the customer's own disclosure — this is arguably the actual root of the later ownership confusion and is more concretely evidenced than treating 05:33 as a clean 'reversal' of 02:03. (4) Add the missed referral-capture moment at 06:47 to the handoff_brief's unresolved_concerns — customer explicitly references neighbors interested in solar (tied to the referral program the rep mentioned at 01:39), and no follow-up action was captured for this. (5) Rebalance the rep_intent evidence at 01:39 — the 'reactive pattern-following' framing versus a plausible strategic referral-capture read isn't evenly weighted; consider revising to genuinely mixed framing rather than leaning negative without support. (6) Button_up citations at 06:57/07:04 should reference the specific missing sub-elements (one_hour_block_stated, no_driving_at_computer, is_that_fair_handshake) individually rather than bundling everything under is_that_fair_handshake.
